result.note: Tests the June 2026 USTR forced-labour tariff proposal against India and the Xinjiang cotton ban under the UFLPA. Section 301 appears only in Sound smarter, so it is not tested.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, the United States Trade Representative (USTR) proposed additional tariffs on Indian imports over forced labour. Consider the following statements about the proposal:
items: The USTR found that India had failed to impose and enforce a ban on imports made with forced labour.
The proposed additional tariff on Indian imports is 25%.
India was the only economy named in the USTR finding.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Only the first statement is correct. The proposed additional tariff is 12.5%, not 25%, and India was named among 60 economies, not alone. The Commerce Ministry stressed the tariffs are not final, with public comments due by 6 July and a hearing on 7 July.
questions.source: The United States Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed an additional 12.5% tariff on Indian imports, naming India among 60 economies it says have failed to curb goods made with forced labour.

questions.prompt: The USTR report of June 2026 on forced labour singled out cotton from which region, whose products the US already bars under its Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act?
questions.explain: The report singled out cotton from China's Xinjiang region, already barred by the US under the UFLPA. Washington's concern is that such forced-labour inputs pass unchecked into India and then move through its supply chains to the US.
questions.source: The report singles out cotton from China’s Xinjiang region, which the US already bars under its Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA).
